Can you confirm:
- If Redwood can issue a Private Offer on AWS that mirrors the attached PO template? (see Nimbus_PO_Template.pdf)

Thanks — can we hop on a quick call tomorrow if needed?

Erin — thanks for the context and the attachments. Looping in Marissa (partner/private-offer lead) and Ben (billing) to confirm the mechanics.

High-level answers up front:
- Yes, we can issue an AWS Private Offer that matches their PO terms in most cases; there are a couple of fields we may need to massage on the PO itself (billing contact and remit address).
- Invoice cadence: if they accept the Private Offer in AWS Marketplace, invoicing is typically managed via our billing team; we can do monthly in arrears or quarterly billing depending on the PO wording. Ben, can you confirm constraints?
- Lead time: Marketplace acceptance takes ~2–5 business days once the Private Offer is created and submitted (seller acceptance window); suggest we start this by Jan 18 to hit Jan 31.

Next steps I propose:
1) Ben to confirm invoice cadence and any PO field requirements.
2) Marissa to draft the Private Offer and send the DocuSign amendment for signatures.
3) Erin / procurement to confirm the PO template fields and return a signed PO if procurement prefers sending a PO rather than signing DocuSign.

If you want, I'll carve out 30 minutes tomorrow to run through acceptance steps end-to-end.

Best,

Thanks Erin — good notes. I'm preparing the AWS Private Offer draft and will mirror the PO fields. A couple of operational notes so procurement knows what to expect: 

- Private Offer flow (seller side):
  1) We create the Private Offer in the AWS Marketplace console with the committed quantity/pricing.
  2) We send the offer to Nimbus's AWS account (they'll receive an email in Marketplace).
  3) Nimbus accepts the offer in their Marketplace console; acceptance triggers the seller to be able to invoice.

- Timing: once we send the offer, acceptance is typically immediate from Nimbus's side but seller-side processing (validating the PO fields and mapping to our billing system) can take 1–3 business days.
- Line items: we'll include a baseline commitment + a separate burst/overage SKU with the rate you specified. Overages will be billed monthly in arrears, committed spend billed quarterly in arrears per your preference.

Attached: RI_SOW_v2.docx (for internal reference), and I'll create the DocuSign amendment (proposed-amendment-docusign.pdf) and link it in HubSpot.

Priyom — I'm going to create the Marketplace offer today. Erin — if procurement can return either: (a) signed PO PDF that matches fields in Nimbus_PO_Template.pdf or (b) accept via Marketplace and send us confirmation, we can close this before month-end.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole

Erin — Ben from billing here. A couple of points from finance: 

- We can support quarterly in arrears for the committed capacity if the PO explicitly states payment terms Net 30 and references HBSP-38271.
- If Nimbus prefers monthly in arrears, we can make that work but it requires the PO to include the billing frequency field and remit address exactly as below (to avoid processing delays):
  Remit: Redwood Inference, 1200 Market St, Suite 400, San Francisco, CA 94103
  Billing contact: billing@redwood.com

- For Marketplace Private Offer acceptance: please send us the Marketplace acceptance confirmation email (screenshot or acceptance ID) — that allows us to tie the acceptance to the HubSpot deal and generate the first invoice.

I'm attaching a signed PO stub template for procurement to populate. If Nimbus can return either the signed PO or accept via Marketplace by Jan 23, we can ensure the Private Offer is live and billable for Feb invoicing.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call if procurement has payment/AR policy questions.

Best,
